title: Software You Don't Need Yet (Stop Overspending)
meta: The features small shops pay for and never use. Buy the boring stuff first — an anti-overspend guide to exactly what to skip until you're actually bigger.
short: Half the features in your plan are for shops twice your size. Here's what to skip until you actually need it.
statLabel: The flashy features gather dust — the boring core pays for itself

body.answer: Most small shops overpay for advanced features they never open — buy the boring core first and add the rest only when you hit a real wall.
body.html:
Software companies are very good at selling you the future. "Imagine when you have ten trucks and need advanced routing." Sure. But you have one truck today, and that advanced routing is a feature you'll pay for every month and open exactly never. The flashy stuff gathers dust. The boring stuff pays for itself. Buy boring first.

This is the article the vendors won't write, because it tells you to spend less. We will, because Booked Job only makes money recommending things that actually fit, and half of what gets upsold doesn't.

body.h2: The boring core that actually earns
body.answer: Scheduling, quoting, invoicing and getting paid are the only features that move money for a small shop — nail those first.
body.html:
Here's what actually earns its place in a small shop: scheduling so you don't double-book, quoting so you're fast and professional, invoicing so you get paid without chasing, and payment so the money lands. That's it. That's the engine. Everything on that list touches a dollar directly. If a feature doesn't clearly help you book a job, do a job, or get paid for a job, it's not core, it's a someday.

Nail those four and you've got most of the value of any platform. The rest is what the sales rep adds to justify a bigger plan.

The test for any feature is dead simple: does it help you book a job, do a job, or get paid for a job? If yes, it's core. If it only helps you analyze, optimize, or automate something you're not even doing at volume yet, it's a someday. Run every line of that plan comparison through that one question and most of the "premium" tier falls away on its own.

body.h2: The stuff to skip until you're bigger
body.answer: Advanced routing, deep reporting dashboards, multi-crew dispatch and marketing automation suites are for shops several sizes up — skip them for now.
body.html:
Here's what small shops pay for and don't use. Advanced multi-crew dispatch, when you are the crew. Deep analytics dashboards, when you can see your whole business in your head. Complex routing optimization, when you run a tight local radius. Full marketing automation suites, when a simple review request would do. None of these are bad features. They're just answers to problems you don't have yet.

The pattern: if a feature solves a problem that only exists at five or ten trucks, it's not for your two. Pay for your size, not your fantasy. When you genuinely grow into those problems, upgrade then, the tools will still be there.

body.h2: Spend the savings where it matters
body.answer: Pick the cheapest plan that covers the boring core, and put the money you saved toward actually getting more customers.
body.html:
So here's the move. Pick the lowest plan that covers scheduling, quoting, invoicing, and payments, cleanly. Skip the tier that unlocks features you can't yet use. Compare plans honestly in the reviews hub, and when you're genuinely unsure whether a feature is core or fluff for your stage, ask someone who's been there.

The money you save by not over-buying software is better spent getting more customers through the door. If you want a straight answer on which plan fits, or where to put that saved money, talk to a human. No upsell, because we're not selling you the software.

faq.q: What software features do small shops actually need?
faq.a: Four: scheduling, quoting, invoicing and payment. Those are the only features that touch a dollar directly for a small shop. Nail them and you've got most of the value of any platform.

faq.q: What should I skip to save money?
faq.a: Advanced routing, deep analytics dashboards, multi-crew dispatch and full marketing automation suites. They solve problems that only exist at five or ten trucks. Pay for your size, not your fantasy.

faq.q: Won't I regret picking a cheaper plan later?
faq.a: No — you can upgrade the day you actually hit the wall, and the advanced features will still be there. Paying now for a problem you don't have yet is just a monthly donation to the software company.
